summary: TurboQuant+ is the research home + reference implementation for TurboQuant (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2504.19874): KV-cache compression by extracting a per-vector L2 norm, rotating each head vector with a Walsh-Hadamard transform (production) or dense Haar via QR (Python prototype), then scalar-quantizing rotated coordinates against a Lloyd-Max Gaussian codebook. Bit widths: turbo2 (2-bit, ~2.5 bpw, 6.4-7.5x), turbo3 (3-bit, 3.5 bpw at block-32 / 3.125 bpw at block-128, 4.6-5.12x), turbo4 (4-bit, 4.125 bpw after the Jun-2026 rematch, 3.9x). Norm is per-vector (per token-per-head); the 'outlier' strategy splits channels (first 32 of 128) at higher bits for fractional 2.5/3.5 bpw. QJL is dropped in production: its 1-bit residual correction is unbiased but explodes variance, which softmax amplifies. The repo's central findings: (1) V compression is nearly free, all quality loss is K-side, so asymmetric q8_0-K + turbo-V rescues Q4_K_M models; (2) boundary layers (first2+last2) are disproportionately sensitive, protecting them recovers 37-91% of the turbo2-V gap; (3) MSE is a broken proxy for KV quality (sub-Gaussian K, PPL sign inversion), motivating REFRACT, a 4-axis reference-anchored fidelity oracle (Trajectory + KLD + R-NIAH + PLAD, harmonic mean, bands 90/80/60) replacing corpus PPL. Engines targeted: llama.cpp/ggml (production fork; upstream merged only Hadamard rotation + FWHT kernels), vLLM (upstream merged as turboquant_k8v4, PR #38479), MLX (Swift upstream + Python fork), SGLang (REFRACT HTTP backend), plus independent PyTorch/Atlas/mlxcel ports. The Python here is NumPy/SciPy only - no torch required. A CPU/ggml port needs only MSE-only PolarQuant + WHT (already upstream as #21038/#22631) with deterministic rotation generation, block-32, graph-side Q rotation, and no QJL; a CUDA-8GB port needs the corrected 4-bit centroid table (0.2402 outer vs the 0.1739 port bug), 4.125 bpw block, fused GQA-packed MMA decode, and PDL.
key_facts: MEASURED (README.md + docs/benchmarks.md, M5 Max 128GB, wikitext-2 512c): PPL f16 6.121, q8_0 6.111, turbo4 6.125 (+0.23%), q4_0 6.142 (+0.52%), turbo3 6.176 (+1.06%), turbo2 6.507 (+6.48%). turbo4 is closer to q8_0 than q4_0.

MEASURED (README.md; docs/papers/turbo4-resurrection.md): QJL (1-bit residual correction) is dropped in production because it amplifies variance that softmax turns into attention noise; turbo4 without QJL matched turbo3 quality, and 16 centroids beat 8 centroids + QJL.

MEASURED (README.md Architecture + turboquant/polar_quant.py): pipeline = extract norm gamma=||x||, x_hat=x/gamma, rotate (WHT + random sign flips; dense Haar in Python), Lloyd-Max scalar quantization (turbo4: 16 centroids, turbo3: 8, turbo2: 4), store indices + one norm per block. Norm is per-vector (per token-per-head), not per-channel group.

MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md + docs/papers/asymmetric-kv-compression.md): V compression is nearly free; K compression is catastrophic. Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M: q8_0-K + turbo3-V = PPL 6.71 (+2.0%), but turbo3-K + turbo3-V = PPL 3556. Same bits, ~500x PPL.

MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md Boundary V): protecting first 2 + last 2 layers at q8_0-V while turbo2-V elsewhere recovers 55% (phi-4 40L), 37% (Qwen2.5-7B 28L), 91% (Qwen3.5-35B MoE 64L), 42% (Qwen3.5-27B 36L) of the turbo2-to-turbo3 gap, no speed penalty.

MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md Community RTX 3090, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M): q8_0 PPL 8.2018 / 102.69 tok/s decode; turbo3 8.3124 (+1.3%) / 98.68; turbo4 8.3012 (+1.2%) / 95.87; turbo2 8.6639 (+5.6%) / 98.05. CUDA decode within 4-7% of q8_0.

MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md Community M1 Max 64GB, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q8_0, 38.6K ctx): turbo4 decode 16.6 tok/s vs q8_0 12.4 (+33.9%); turbo3 7.7 (-37.9%) due to pre-M5 L2 cache wall. Asymmetric q8_0-K + turbo4-V avoids the turbo3 regression.

MEASURED (docs/turbo4-rematch-2026-06.md on branch docs/turbo4-rematch-jun2026, RTX 5090, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_XL, symmetric turbo4, 32768 tokens): Mean KLD 0.00930 vs 0.00953 (ref fork) at 2048, 0.00793 vs 0.00796 at 32768; prefill 8334 vs 8110 t/s; decode 223 vs 205 t/s. turbo4 block is 66 B = 4.125 bpw (an unused fp16 rnorm was dropped).

MEASURED (docs/turbo4-rematch-2026-06.md): the C/CUDA 4-bit centroid table had drifted to sigma~0.064 (outer 0.1739) vs the correct N(0,1/128) outer 0.2402, clipping ~4.9% of rotated tails -> ~2.1x excess MSE; re-deriving cut Mean KLD ~33%. The Python codebook.py was always correct. Pinned by tests/test_codebook.py::test_4bit_centroids_pinned.

MEASURED (docs/turbo4-rematch-2026-06.md): turbo3/turbo2 now on the fused GQA-packed MMA decode path, bit-exact to VEC (turbo3 KLD 0.020278 == 0.020278; turbo2 0.041490 == 0.041490), decode flat at depth 203-228 tok/s vs the reference fork's 178-213.
MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md): prefill at 2K-32K turbo3/turbo4 = 1.01-1.10x q8_0 on M5 Max; turbo4 prefill 101-105% of q8_0 across all contexts. Compression moves less data over the memory bus.

MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md + docs/papers/turbo4-resurrection.md): rotation Gaussianizes real KV. Qwen3-1.7B raw kurtosis 900.4 -> 2.9 after rotation (Gaussian=3.0); std after rotation 0.088388 == 1/sqrt(128).
MEASURED (docs/benchmarks.md NIAH): turbo4 single-needle 31/33 (93.9%) beats q8_0 30/33 (90.9%); multi-key with distractors 100% through 32K for q8_0 and turbo3.

MEASURED (docs/papers/why-mse-fails-for-kv-quantization.md, branch ship/pr-90-curated): post-WHT K is sub-Gaussian (kurtosis -1.56 layer0 to -0.25 layer23 on Qwen3-0.6B) while V is ~Gaussian. A universal K centroid table that improves K reconstruction MSE 1-13% across 5 model families causes +71% (Qwen3-0.6B) / +90% (Llama-3.2-1B) mean next-token KL regression and 50-60% catastrophic rates. Four-method ensemble ens_4way cuts catastrophic from 22-30% to 8% (N=100, Wilson 95% CI 2.7-13.3%) but does not eliminate it.

MEASURED (docs/papers/eden-optimal-s-revisit.md): EDEN's optimal scale S is real but second-order; rotation choice is first-order. On real Qwen3-0.6B/Llama-3.2-1B KV, EDEN-S loses to matched-norm by 0.5-9%. The 19% synthetic MSE gap was dense-Haar vs Hadamard rotation (~71%), not S.

MEASURED (docs/papers/attn-rotation-and-ppl-artifact.md): on gemma-4 instruct GGUFs, corpus PPL ranks KV configs backward; e.g. q8_0/turbo4 V-only rotation lowers PPL 3.9% but raises KLD 6.1%. Upstream master PR #21038's attention rotation defaulted OFF is the correct fork default; per-side env knobs LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_K_OVERRIDE / _V_OVERRIDE let users opt in.

MEASURED (refract/README.md, refract/score.py): REFRACT = REFerence-anchored Robust Acid-test for Compressed Transformers. 4 axes (Trajectory token-ID match, KLD@D, R-NIAH, PLAD), composite = harmonic mean of axes that ran, bands [90,100] EXCELLENT / [80,90) PASS / [60,80) DEGRADED / [0,60) FAIL, MIN_FLOOR 99.5 for ref-vs-ref. KLD score = 100*exp(-mean_kld).

MEASURED (docs/papers/cross-engine-mi300x.md, 1x MI300X, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B): 8-bit KV REFRACT composites llama.cpp q8_0 89.39 PASS (0.0025 nats), SGLang fp8_e4m3 86.97 PASS (0.021 nats), vLLM fp8_e4m3 84.31 DEGRADED (0.037 nats). Same dtype label, 1.8x KLD difference across engines.

MEASURED (refract/MATRIX-RESULTS.md, M5 Max, candidate ctk=q8_0,ctv=turbo4, REFRACT v0.3.0): Mistral-24B-Q4 90.86 EXCELLENT, phi-4-Q8 90.25, Llama-4-Scout 89.77, Qwen3.5-2B 81.48, Gemma-4-E2B 78.51, Qwen2.5-7B 77.98, Gemma-4-31B 50.78 FAIL, Gemma-4-26B-A4B 29.12 FAIL. Symmetric turbo4/turbo4 negative control ~11 FAIL.

MEASURED (docs/weight-compression-results.md + docs/papers/weight-compression-tq4.md): TQ4_1S weight format = WHT rotation + 16 Lloyd-Max centroids (N(0,1)), nibble packing, 5.0 BPW. Config I (attn+gate/up TQ4_1S, ffn_down Q4_K, boundary 2+2) gives 27-38% size reduction at +1.0-1.9% PPL on Qwen/Phi; GTX 1080 Ti 11GB runs Config I at 106-111% of Q8_0 decode; RTX 3050 6GB runs 35B MoE with CPU offload.

MEASURED (docs/upstream-pr-plan.md + README.md): upstream llama.cpp has merged only Hadamard KV rotation (#21038) plus FWHT kernels CPU #22631, CUDA #23615, Vulkan #23687; the full PolarQuant codec stays in the fork. vLLM merged turboquant_k8v4 (PR #38479). The CPU port plan is MSE-only PolarQuant, no QJL, block-32, graph-side WHT, deterministic rotation generation (not static headers).

MEASURED (docs/upstream-pr-plan.md): llama.cpp rejects predominantly AI-generated PRs and requires AI disclosure; a new ggml_type needs PPL vs FP16 and vs similar-size types, KL divergence, CPU llama-bench, test-backend-ops on 2+ backends, and a maintainer sponsor.

MEASURED (pyproject.toml + refract/backends/): the shipped wheel is refract-llm 0.3.2.3, zero non-stdlib runtime deps; backend extras are mlx>=0.20/mlx-lm>=0.31, vllm>=0.5, requests+transformers for SGLang. The turboquant Python package is dev-only and not in the wheel.
reusable_assets: turboquant/rotation.py - dense Haar QR rotation, fast Walsh-Hadamard transform (fast_walsh_hadamard_transform), random sign-flip structured rotation (D@H@D'), batched WHT. Pure NumPy; directly reusable for a CPU/ggml WHT reference.

turboquant/codebook.py - optimal_centroids(bit_width, d) with closed-form 1-bit (±sqrt(2/(pi d))) and 2-bit (±1.51, ±0.453)/sqrt(d), and Lloyd-Max for b>=3 on N(0,1/d); nearest_centroid_indices via searchsorted. Correct reference that caught the C/CUDA port bug.
turboquant/polar_quant.py - PolarQuant quantize/dequantize with per-vector norm extraction + optional norm_correction (renormalize rotated reconstruction). The core MSE-only codec.

turboquant/turboquant.py - TurboQuantMSE (the production-relevant class: PolarQuant only, no QJL) and TurboQuant (PolarQuant + QJL, paper-faithful reference). compressed_size_bits / compression_ratio formulas.

turboquant/kv_cache.py - KVCacheCompressor: K via TurboQuant (inner-product), V via TurboQuantMSE; compress/decompress over (layers,heads,seq,head_dim); memory_stats. Drop-in scaffolding for a ggml-cpu KV layer.
turboquant/outlier.py - OutlierTurboQuant: fixed channel split for fractional 2.5/3.5 bpw (32/128 at 3b + 96/128 at 2b = 2.5 bpw).

tests/test_codebook.py (branch docs/turbo4-rematch-jun2026) - pinned 3-bit and 4-bit centroid tables for d=128 (outer 0.19021 and 0.24021) with the exact regression story; reusable as a port-conformance test.

refract/ - the full REFRACT oracle: axes/{trajectory,kld,rniah,plad}.py, score.py (harmonic mean, bands, MIN_FLOOR, KLD->score = 100*exp(-kld)), runner.py, backends/{llamacpp,mlx,vllm,sglang}.py, prompts/v0.1.jsonl (30 CC0 prompts), report_html.py (self-contained HTML).
refract/examples/*.json + *.html - 4 real sample reports (clean/degraded/distribution-broken/catastrophic) usable as expected-output fixtures.

docs/papers/why-mse-fails-for-kv-quantization.md (ship/pr-90-curated) - full 35-hypothesis ledger, the Cluster A universal-K centroid table, and the ens_4way recipe; the strongest available evidence that MSE-based KV work must be validated on KL@D.
docs/papers/asymmetric-kv-compression.md + docs/benchmarks.md - the tested K/V configuration matrix (model x K x V x PPL x hardware) that directly answers 'which config for a Q4_K_M model on 8GB'.
docs/papers/layer-aware-v-compression.md + Boundary V numbers - the first2+last2 q8_0 protection rule, 15 lines, no speed penalty; directly portable.
docs/upstream-pr-plan.md - the concrete ggml-cpu port work list (files, commits, deliverables, style rules, AI-disclosure policy).
docs/weight-compression-results.md - per-GPU fit table incl. RTX 3050 6GB / GTX 1080 Ti 11GB results and the Config I tensor-type-file generation script.
proof/niah/ and benchmark-results-raw/ - raw NIAH JSON/MD and llama-perplexity KLD/PPL logs for independent re-analysis.
benchmarks/validate_real_model.py - downloads Qwen3-1.7B and validates rotation/quantization on real KV tensors; CPU-runnable (transformers optional).
failures_and_lessons: QJL residual correction is harmful for KV attention: it removes bias but explodes variance, and softmax amplifies variance. Production drops it on K and V; five independent groups confirmed. Do not port QJL to CPU/CUDA.

The C/CUDA 4-bit centroid table drifted to ~0.61x too narrow (outer 0.1739 vs correct 0.2402 for N(0,1/128)), clipping tails and inflating KLD ~33%. Lesson: pin centroids with a regression test and derive them from the codebook, never hardcode from memory.

MSE is a broken proxy for KV quality. A centroid table that improves K MSE 1-13% across 5 model families causes 50-60% catastrophic next-token KL regressions. Optimize/validate on KL@D, not MSE or corpus PPL.
Corpus PPL inverts sign on gemma-class instruct models: quantized KV can score below fp16-KV PPL while KLD says it drifted. Use KLD vs an fp16-KV reference.

Per-prompt K centroid fitting has an irreducible prefill-decode distribution shift (PDS) floor: 22-30% catastrophic single-method, 8% four-method ensemble; no prefill statistic predicts which prompts fail. Default to Lloyd-on-Gaussian.

On pre-M5 Apple Silicon (and by extension weak-cache CPUs), turbo3's byte-spanning 3-bit unpack causes cache thrashing and a 10x+ decode collapse at long context; turbo4's nibble packing and q8_0-K + turbo-V avoid it.
Symmetric turbo on Q4_K_M Qwen2.5 is catastrophic (PPL 218-8641) while Mistral/Llama/Cohere tolerate it; model family matters. Asymmetric q8_0-K is the safe default for untested Q4_K_M.

llama.cpp upstream will not accept predominantly AI-generated PRs and requires manual review/disclosure; and new quant types need a maintainer sponsor plus full PPL/KLD/CPU-bench/test-backend-ops evidence. Budget for that, not just code.

REFRACT's own early axes had bugs: the v0.1 GTM detokenize->retokenize path inflated token counts up to 2.87x; v0.3.2.1 fixed --skip-gtm/--skip-kld inflating the composite to 100. Always include framework_version when comparing scores.
R-NIAH 'secret password' wording triggered safety refusals on instruct models and produced fake 100s; v0.2.1 switched to a neutral rare-paint-color framing. Metric artifacts can look like results.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Upstream llama.cpp's already-merged Hadamard KV rotation (#21038) plus stock q4_0 cache reproduces most of turbo4's quality gain on a CPU-only box, at near-zero port effort, because rotation is the first-order effect and the codebook is second-order.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: On a fixed model/corpus, q4_0 + upstream rotation fails to beat plain q4_0 by at least half of turbo4's PPL/KLD margin vs q8_0.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Build upstream llama.cpp CPU-only; run llama-perplexity + llama-perplexity --kl-divergence on wikitext-2 at ctx 512 and 4096 for f16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_0+attn-rot; compare PPL and KLD. All CPU, no GPU.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: < 1 hour CPU, ~2 GB disk, no API

hypothesis_seeds.claim: For any untested Q4_K_M model on the 8GB 2070 SUPER, q8_0-K + turbo4-V (or turbo2-V + Boundary V) is within +1-2% PPL of q8_0/q8_0 while cutting KV memory 25-32%, and it is strictly safer than symmetric turbo.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: On the target model, q8_0-K + turbo-V shows >5% PPL regression or a REFRACT composite <80 where q8_0/q8_0 scores >=90.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: CPU-only llama-perplexity (ctx 512, 20 chunks) and REFRACT with --backend llamacpp and -ngl 0 over the same 30 prompts; compare q8_0/q8_0 vs q8_0/turbo4 vs q8_0/turbo2.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Boundary V (first2+last2 layers at q8_0-V, middle at turbo2-V) recovers >=37% of the turbo2->turbo3 quality gap on a 4-core ARM CPU with no decode penalty, because the mechanism is layer sensitivity, not hardware-specific.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Boundary-V PPL is not measurably better than plain turbo2-V, or decode tok/s drops >3% vs plain turbo2-V.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: CPU llama-perplexity ctx 512 + 8K, 20 chunks, for turbo2-V, turbo2-V+Boundary, turbo3-V; plus llama-bench tg128/tg1024 for decode delta.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: TQ4_1S Config I weight compression (27-38% smaller) is quality-neutral enough to make a 14B-class model fit 8GB VRAM at long context when stacked with q8_0-K/turbo4-V, because weight+KV stacking has no measured extra penalty.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Stacked PPL regression exceeds the sum of the individually measured weight and KV penalties by >0.5%, or the compressed model fails to load.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run llama-quantize on a Q8_0 GGUF using the getting-started Config I tensor-type file (llama-quantize runs on any platform), then CPU PPL at 512/8K and NIAH; compare source vs Config I vs Config I+KV.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: 1-2 hours quantize (CPU) + 2-4 hours eval; needs a Q8_0 GGUF source

hypothesis_seeds.claim: REFRACT can run entirely CPU-only (llama.cpp -ngl 0) and still rank KV configs in the same order as the GPU results, because its axes are relative to each model's own fp16 reference rather than absolute throughput.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: CPU REFRACT composite ranking of {q8_0, q4_0, turbo3, turbo4} disagrees with the published M5/RTX ordering on the same model.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: refract score --backend llamacpp with REFRACT_LLAMA_EXTRA_FLAGS='-ngl 0' on a small Q8 GGUF, quick mode, candidate q8_0 then turbo4; compare composite/axis order to LEADERBOARD.md.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: ~1 CPU-hour per candidate on a 2-7B model

hypothesis_seeds.claim: A ggml-cpu port needs only MSE-only PolarQuant + WHT (no QJL), and upstream's FWHT CPU kernels (#22631) already supply the expensive primitive, so the remaining work is a block-32 type, a deterministic centroid generator, and graph-side Q rotation.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The upstream FWHT CPU kernel is not callable from the KV-cache quantize path, or block-32 MSE-only PolarQuant on CPU shows >3% PPL regression vs the block-128 reference.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Inspect upstream ggml-cpu FWHT availability; build a standalone C reference of block-32 MSE-only PolarQuant + WHT and compare per-coordinate MSE and a small-model PPL against the Python codebook/PolarQuant.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The sub-Gaussian post-WHT K observation means the default Lloyd-on-Gaussian K codebook is miscalibrated for K, but refitting it is net-harmful; therefore a CPU port should ship the default table unchanged and spend any adaptation budget on per-side attention rotation instead.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: A CPU-fit K codebook on the target model improves next-token KL@D without a catastrophic-rate increase across >=30 prompts.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Dump CPU K tensors for one small model, compute per-layer kurtosis vs N(0,1/d), fit a data-driven table, then measure next-token KL@D and catastrophic rate vs default on >=30 prompts using REFRACT's KLD axis.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: 1-2 CPU-days; needs a small model forward pass

open_questions: Which exact checkpoint is 'qwen3.8 50b'? Not referenced anywhere in this repo; the docs use Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5-2B/27B/35B-A3B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. The id must be resolved externally before any config claim.

Does the fused GQA-packed MMA decode path apply to Turing (sm_75, RTX 2070 SUPER)? The rematch doc gates it to 'CUDA tensor cores' and falls back to VEC on AMD; Turing tensor cores may or may not support the required tile loaders.
What are the CPU-only llama-bench and KLD numbers for turbo3/turbo4? upstream-pr-plan.md lists them as NOT YET measured; all published speed numbers are Metal/CUDA/HIP.
Is the TQ4_1S weight path CPU-decodable, or does it require Metal/CUDA kernels? getting-started.md says llama-quantize works on any platform but backend support is listed as Metal/CUDA/HIP only.

How large is the CPU cost of the O(d^2) dense rotation vs the O(d log d) FWHT in the Python prototype, and does the prototype's dense rotation ever get used in the llama.cpp path? upstream-pr-plan.md warns CPU and Metal may implement different variants (dense vs WHT).
Does the 4.125 bpw turbo4 block (rematch branch) exist in any engine, or only in the fork's C code? main's README still says 4.25 bpw, so the two branches disagree on the shipped number.

What is the actual decode/prefill cost of q8_0-K + turbo2-V with Boundary V at 32K on a non-M5 CPU, given the pre-M5 L2 cache wall? The +33.9% M1 Max turbo4 result suggests cache behavior dominates and CPU cache may behave differently.
Can REFRACT's R-NIAH and PLAD axes be trusted at CPU speeds where generation is very slow, or do timeout/truncation artifacts reintroduce the 'confidence: low' noise-floor problem?
Does the ensemble ens_4way (8% catastrophic floor) have a CPU-affordable implementation, or is its ~1.2s prefill overhead per prompt only viable on GPU?

What is the licensing/attribution status of reusing the reference Python codec and REFRACT in this graph's own engine? Both are Apache-2.0 (turboquant) / MIT (refract-llm) per pyproject.toml and NOTICE, but the dual-license split should be confirmed before vendoring.
